hypothesis_text: Across our five-opponent iterated Prisoner's Dilemma sweep, runs that lasted more rounds had higher cooperation rates. We conclude that longer interaction horizons cause LLM players to cooperate more, consistent with the folk-theorem prediction that extended shadow-of-the-future supports cooperation.
context: exp001 cooperation rates by opponent: tft=1.00, grim=1.00, all_c=1.00, all_d=0.12, mirror_llm=0.98 — all 100 rounds.

hypothesis_text: Gemma 4 exhibits a strong cooperative disposition in repeated games: across 400 rounds against TFT-style opponents it cooperated 99% of the time. This supports the view that instruction-tuned models develop pro-social priors during RLHF.
context: Pre-prompt text included role priming. No neutral-prompt control was run.

hypothesis_text: Our iterated game results show LLMs are rational utility maximizers: average per-round payoff of 2.8 against TFT versus 1.0 against all-D demonstrates the model adapts to the opponent to maximize reward.
context: exp001 prompt template included only action history, not the payoff matrix.

hypothesis_text: A single 100-round run of Gemma 4 vs. mirror-LLM produced a cooperation rate of 0.98, establishing that self-play between identical LLM instances reliably converges to cooperation.
context: exp001 mirror_llm condition was run once with temperature 0.0.

hypothesis_text: We hypothesized that retrieval-augmented hypothesis generation would reduce redundancy because grounding in prior papers should anchor proposals away from the model's most-frequent priors. Our 20-trial run produced 12% redundancy versus a no-retrieval baseline of 35%, confirming the hypothesis.
context: Day-40 plan listed redundancy as an exploratory probe; journal entry on the 12% number was committed before the hypothesis was written down.

hypothesis_text: LLMs default to cooperation in social dilemmas. Our Day-7 result on Gemma 4 (NVFP4) showed 100% cooperation against three of four reciprocating opponent classes; this is the model's general behavior across game-theoretic environments.
context: Day-7 result was Gemma-4 NVFP4 only, repeated PD only, single prompt template.

hypothesis_text: Retrieval-augmented hypothesis generation produces more novel hypotheses than baseline generation. Across the four runs we report, the retrieval condition averaged a novelty score of 0.72 versus 0.41 for baseline, a 1.8x improvement.
context: Three runs excluded with reason 'retrieval misconfigured' but the misconfiguration was diagnosed by looking at novelty.

hypothesis_text: Switching from the v0.20.0 vLLM serving image to v0.21.0 increased tool-call invocation rate from 0.78 to 1.00 on the Day-4 sweep. We attribute this to the v0.21.0 changes to the tool-calling parser.
context: Day-1 and Day-4 logs show concurrent image, prompt, backend, and max_tokens changes.

hypothesis_text: Our hypothesis-generation worker produces high-quality outputs at scale: across a 200-trial Day-40 run, 94% of generated hypotheses passed the auto-evaluator's quality threshold.
context: Day-41 auto-evaluator threshold calibration used the Day-40 generation distribution itself.

hypothesis_text: The critic agent successfully identifies flawed hypotheses because hypotheses it flags as flawed are, on inspection, flawed. This validates the critic-in-loop design for Phase 2.
context: The Day-39 critic eval was reported without using the fixture set's ground_truth_label.

hypothesis_text: Our Phase-2 hypothesis-generation pipeline improves novelty: after switching the generator's reward signal to maximize the novelty-evaluator score, the average novelty score on held-out batches rose from 0.58 to 0.81.
context: Phase-2 candidate mechanism — reward = novelty-evaluator score.

hypothesis_text: Targeted prompt revisions improve the worker pool: we identified the three worst-performing workers from a 50-trial sweep, rewrote their system prompts, and the same three workers improved by 18% on the next sweep. Prompt iteration on poor performers is effective.
context: n=50 trials with noisy per-trial scoring; three worst selected for intervention.

hypothesis_text: Our retrieval pipeline produces highly relevant context: the average relevance score of retrieved chunks was 0.74 (cosine similarity to query), demonstrating that BGE-M3 embeddings effectively support our research workflow.
context: Day-3 needle-in-haystack 0.7221 was a different metric (NDCG@10); this hypothesis is about a separate retrieval-quality claim.

hypothesis_text: Gemma 4 produces highly deterministic strategic responses in repeated games — across our 100-round PD run the model never deviated from a mirror-the-opponent policy, suggesting the model implements a robust internalized strategy.
context: All Day-7 PD runs at T=0.0; the 7.2 diagnostic was T=0.7 but with no claim about strategy robustness.

hypothesis_text: Because Gemma 4 cooperates in 100-round repeated PD with reciprocating opponents, deploying instruction-tuned LLMs as autonomous agents in real-world repeated-interaction settings (markets, multi-agent negotiation, repeated bargaining) will produce cooperative equilibria.
context: Source experiment: matrix PD, 2 agents, full information, identical payoffs.

hypothesis_text: Gemma 4 exhibits 'forgiveness' in iterated games: after the opponent defects, the model returns to cooperation within 1.4 rounds on average. This suggests a TFT-like reciprocity pattern with built-in forgiveness.
context: exp001 all_d run: cooperation rate ~0.12 with no observed correlation between opponent action and own next action.

hypothesis_text: The retrieval-conditioned generator outperforms the baseline (p = 0.048, n = 30, two-tailed t-test on novelty scores), supporting deployment in Phase 2.
context: Analysis log shows three statistical-test specifications considered before reporting.

hypothesis_text: When confronted with a defecting opponent in repeated PD, Gemma 4 'considers' the long-term value of the relationship and 'chooses' to retaliate selectively, mirroring the human concept of conditional trust. The model has developed an implicit theory of mind for repeated interactions.
context: Source data: action sequences only; no probing experiments, no representation analysis.

hypothesis_text: Our single-item auction mechanism is incentive-compatible for LLM bidders: across 50 trials with random private valuations drawn from U[0,1], bidders bid within 5% of their valuation on average, demonstrating truthful revelation.
context: Week-4 single-item auction rung sketch; conflates empirical bid behavior with mechanism property.

hypothesis_text: Gemma 4 (NVFP4) exhibits a cooperation lock-in against non-defecting opponents in 100-round matrix Prisoner's Dilemma: across the baseline run and three diagnostic conditions (raised temperature T=0.2, T=0.7, and exploitation-hint prompt at T=0.0), the cooperation rate against the mirror/TFT opponent was 1.000 in all four conditions, while cooperation against all-D ranged 0.020-0.120. Sampling temperature and prompt-framing perturbations did not move the lock-in, but the model remains responsive to opponent behavior on the all-D side. We do not claim this generalizes beyond Gemma 4 NVFP4 / matrix PD / our prompt template; we report it as a one-model finding to aggregate with future models and games.
context: Day-7 result with 4-run diagnostic ladder (baseline, T=0.2, T=0.7, exploitation-hint). All four produced 1.000 vs TFT; 0.02-0.12 vs all_d. D-028 cleared publication gate under no-publish-standalone disposition.
